7 Brew Pink Paradise Lemonade: Price & Calories

A medium Pink Paradise Lemonade is about $3.50, with 270 calories, 0 mg of caffeine and 65 g of sugar. Every number here comes from 7 Brew's own published nutrition guide, broken out by size and preparation.

Pink Paradise Lemonade allergens

7 Brew's published allergen guide lists no declared allergens for the standard Pink Paradise Lemonade. Adding a milk, syrup or topping changes this, and every drink is made on shared equipment, so cross-contact is possible.

If you are ordering around an allergy, check the full allergen and dietary guide and confirm at the window.

How to order a Pink Paradise Lemonade

Ask for it by name — it is on the standard board at every 7 Brew, so no special script is needed. Say the size first, then the drink: "Can I get a medium Pink Paradise Lemonade?"

Worth knowing before you order: the base is customisable. You can swap milk, ask for sugar-free syrups, change the sweetness level, or have most drinks made iced, hot or blended as a frozen chiller where the menu allows. Ordering through the app earns 100 rewards points either way.

Make a Pink Paradise Lemonade at Home

Honest note first: no official ratio is published for this drink, and no fan page prints measured amounts. Here is a starting ratio that lands close. Adjust by fruit, not by sugar.

For one large glass

  • 1 1/2 cups lemonade
  • 1 teaspoon cherry syrup
  • 1 teaspoon watermelon syrup
  • 1 teaspoon raspberry syrup
  • A squeeze of fresh lemon at the end
  • A full cup of ice
  1. Syrups into the lemonade, stir well. The color should go properly pink, darker than bottled pink lemonade.
  2. Ice in, then the squeeze of lemon. That squeeze is the regulars' trick from the stand version too: half sweet, extra lemon.
  3. Taste in order. Cherry first? Good. Watermelon rounding it? Good. Raspberry still there at the end? Done.

Lighter build: half the syrups and keep the lemon squeeze. The tartness does the work the sugar was doing.

7 Brew Pink Paradise Lemonade FAQ

How many calories are in a 7 Brew Pink Paradise Lemonade?

A medium iced Pink Paradise Lemonade has 270 calories. A small has 200 and a large 400, according to 7 Brew's nutrition guide.

How much caffeine is in a 7 Brew Pink Paradise Lemonade?

0 mg. Cherry, watermelon, raspberry and lemonade carry no caffeine.

How much does a 7 Brew Pink Paradise Lemonade cost?

Roughly $2.75 for a small, $3.50 for a medium and $4.25 for a large. Prices are our estimates and vary by stand — every 7 Brew is independently owned.

How much sugar is in a 7 Brew Pink Paradise Lemonade?

65 g in a medium.

What flavors are in Pink Paradise Lemonade, in what order?

Cherry, watermelon, raspberry. That is the official order on 7 Brew's menu, and it is also the order you taste them: cherry bold up front, watermelon softening the middle, raspberry tart and lingering at the end. It needs saying because the guides scramble it. The top fan guide lists raspberry, cherry, watermelon. Even Google's snippet for that guide describes this drink as raspberry and smooth coconut. There is no coconut in Pink Paradise. Coconut lives in the Cocoberry. Three fruits, one base, no coconut.

What did Tasting Table think of Pink Paradise?

They liked it. Tasting Table tried all six new lemonades on launch day in May 2026 and scored the lineup five hits and one miss. Pink Paradise was a hit. The miss was the Blackberry Cobbler Lemon Freeze. Their reviewer called it darker and more complex than a typical pink lemonade, sweet and ultra-juicy with a little tartness, and landed the funniest verdict in the whole series: this drink reminded her more of a fruit roll-up than the actual Fruit Roll-Up Lemonade did. Her one caution was sweetness. Treat drink, not a daily driver.

Is there a sugar-free Pink Paradise Lemonade?

No. The guide publishes no sugar-free Pink Paradise, same as its lemonade siblings. One of the top guides lists a sugar-free version under its sweetness options anyway. It did the same thing on the Fruit Roll-Up page, for a drink that cannot be built sugar-free either. What actually works, and what regulars order: half sweet or quarter sweet, with extra lemon squeezed in. The tartness carries the lighter build, and light ice keeps it from diluting into pink water. The full set of drinks with a real sugar-free version lives on our sugar-free page.

Why does one guide say a medium has 38 to 58 g of sugar?

Because that guide estimated instead of reading. Its medium range tops out at 58 g, and the official figure is 65 g, so the real drink sits above its entire range. Ranges feel safe to publish, but a range that excludes the truth is just a wrong number with company. The guide's figures are the ones in the table above: 270 calories and 65 g of sugar in a medium iced, 200 and 49 in a small, 400 and 98 in a large.

Pink Paradise or Pink Mermaid: are they the same drink?

No, and the shared pink causes real mix-ups at the window. This one is a lemonade: cherry, watermelon and raspberry in still lemonade. Pink Mermaid is a 7 Fizz: watermelon, coconut and strawberry in sparkling soda water. Different base, different trio, different texture. If you want juicy and smooth, order Paradise. If you want light and bubbly, order Mermaid. Both are caffeine-free.
